lead_headline: Workflow SDK closes a coordinated replay and event-integrity push; AI SDK ships two new first-party providers
lead_body: Workflow SDK spent the day closing replay correctness work — stable-turn gating, hook-payload buffering, VM-idle counter backport — then hardened production contracts: fatal world failures, per-(run, correlation) uniqueness in world-postgres, and parent WritableStream passthrough to child workflows. AI SDK matched the pace with 31 commits, adding @ai-sdk/anthropic-aws and @ai-sdk/quiverai alongside Google search grounding in generateImage and an MCP auth-refresh dedup fix.
lead_article:
The day's heaviest lift belongs to Workflow SDK, which closed out a string of replay-system commits before midnight — waiting for a stable workflow turn before resuming, yielding replay after buffering hook payloads, backporting a VM-idle replay counter — then layered production-grade hardening on top: world contract failures now captured as fatal, per-(run, correlation) uniqueness enforced for entity-creating events in world-postgres, and a late commit adding support for passing a parent WritableStream down to a child workflow via start(). The world-vercel PR switching event endpoints to the v4 wire format rounds out a day that reads less like incremental polish and more like a coordinated push toward replay correctness and strict event integrity.

AI SDK was the other high-volume project, shipping two new first-party providers — @ai-sdk/anthropic-aws at v1.0.0 and @ai-sdk/quiverai at v2.0.0 — alongside Google search grounding support in generateImage, an OpenAI fix that skips passing reasoning items when a previous response ID is present, and an MCP auth-refresh deduplication patch on the HTTP transport. Astro had a clean release day: astro@6.3.7 and @astrojs/cloudflare@13.5.4 both shipped, carrying fixes for the misleading redirect error, custom elements in MDX bypassing the renderer pipeline, and Node adapter buffer bodies being JSON-stringified instead of passed through. Claude Code cut two releases — v2.1.146 and v2.1.147 — while absorbing a heavy inflow of issues ranging from a file descriptor leak regression in large monorepos to worktree isolation failures and MCP approval-gate breakage in scheduled routines. Hydrogen and Metaflow were quiet: a single i18n replacer fix in Hydrogen, a dependency bump and a pair of Batch-related issues in Metaflow. The Gemma.cpp PR adding a direct HuggingFace safetensors loader for Gemma 4 E2B/E4B is worth watching — small surface area, but it removes a friction point that currently makes local Gemma 4 experimentation more cumbersome than it needs to be.
